stem:
Kabir looks at the diagram. Ray $OA$ and ray $OB$ meet at $O$ and form $\angle AOB$. A full turn around $O$ is split into $360$ equal parts.

Which claim correctly assigns a degree measure to $\angle AOB$?

options.text: The measure is the count of those equal one-degree parts that lie between ray $OA$ and ray $OB$.
The measure is the printed letter $O$ at the vertex, read as the degree number.
Any count of parts between the rays is a degree measure, even if the parts of the full turn are unequal.
Counting one-degree parts between the rays is what creates the full $360$-part turn.

teacher.key_rationale: A degree is one of 360 equal parts of a full turn; the angle measure is how many of those equal parts fit between the arms. Letter height is not a measure. Unequal parts break the unit. The turn definition is not produced by counting one angle.
teacher.figure_note: Added angle AOB at O with rays OA, OB and an arc mark for the interior angle.
